newsitem.title: UK: Ofgas won't widen TransCo reference yet.
newsitem.headline: Ofgas won't widen TransCo reference yet.

text.p: Industry regulator Ofgas on Monday said it would not ask the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) to investigate structural changes at British Gas, but instead focus solely on the controversial price proposals for pipeline unit TransCo.
The regulator added, however, it might widen the terms of the investigation at a later stage.
The initiative for a wider investigation would have to come from the MMC, an Ofgas spokesman said.
The regulator said last week it was considering widening the reference after British Gas rejected Ofgas' final price proposals for TransCo and demanded them to be vetted by the MMC.
Industry watchers feared a broader investigation would hamper British Gas' plan to split itself in two early next year.
The utility plans to demerge into British Gas Energy, which will house the trading business and domestic production interests, and a separate company, called TransCo International.
TransCo International would not only include British Gas' regulated transport and storage activities, but also its foreign production and power generation operations.
Press reports had suggested Ofgas might want the MMC to investigate whether the two businesses within TransCo International should in some way be separated.
But an Ofgas spokesman said the regulator considered a wider investigation inapproriate at this stage.
"We've only been dealing with price control and it would be inapproriate to go beyond that at this stage," the spokesman said.
"We have no intention of widening the investigation," he added.
Ofgas has asked the MMC to conclude its investigation into TransCo's price regime within six months.
Ofgas proposed that TransCo would cut charges to gas suppliers by 20 percent in 1997 and then by 6.5 percent below inflation for the following four years.
British Gas said earlier the proposals would leave it with insufficient money to invest adequately in its infrastructure,, adding they would cut the unit's cash flow by 400 million stg.
It also feared thousands of job losses if the proposals were implemented.
But Ofgas said the current price regime provided British Gas with more money than it needed to operate its pipelines.
